sentences.text: Researchers used mice to investigate how the breakdown of motor memories is connected to the removal of specific myelin sheaths by microglia.
When cells involved in motor memory become less active, the surrounding myelin-producing cells produce less of a protective signal called CD47, which allows microglia to eat the myelin.
Removing the CD47 signal from these myelin-producing cells sped up the loss of motor memory, while boosting the signal had the opposite effect.
The research found that microglia remove myelin sheaths and synapses through separate, independent processes.
Because different kinds of memory rely on myelination, the authors suggest this process might also help explain how other types of memories fade.
